originality.rationale: No exact weighted commuting-neighborhood census of characteristic-two idempotent associative derivations was found. The strongest recent finite-field G-grading classification applies to individual gradings with all finite subgroups cyclic, whereas commuting pairs yield the noncyclic Klein-four grading compatibility problem. Britnell–Wildon and Fulman–Guralnick analyze much broader or differently quantified matrix pairs. The new central-commutator lemma and Artin–Schreier centralizer fibers give the nontrivial degree distribution. The claim is restricted to this pair-degree formula and provisional concerning unpublished or unread stronger general results.
residual_risks: The potentially dominating arXiv:2610.20113 full text was unavailable; its abstract does not establish the paired result, but an unadvertised compatible-pair theorem cannot be ruled out.
A broader enumeration of simultaneous semisimple matrix pairs or full Klein-four gradings may imply the formula; no exhaustive publication-priority guarantee.

value.rationale: The complete valency distribution and ordered-pair count are intrinsic invariants of the natural commuting graph on projection derivations, for all dimensions and finite fields. It detects an arithmetic quadratic-extension stratum invisible in ordinary unweighted gradings, giving precise structural information beyond any isolated small example. Potential future use includes graph invariants, simultaneous grading compatibility, and comparison between algebras.
